summary:
PASS 1 grind (2026-08-04): re-measured every non-match item against the CURRENT tree — it had moved substantially since this map was written (owner-review-1 and the search/settings passes had already fixed the rail search icon and the +new dialog; both were re-verified live and flipped to match). What remained: the message queue (built for real — client-side hold/reorder/edit/remove state plus a genuinely wired 'interrupt and deliver' backed by POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel, not a mock); the composer's ask-button mode-reset bug (one-line fix, confirmed via a failing-first test); and the shared window chrome (Layer.tsx maximize/pop-out/close, the detail-slot's Copy/Download/Maximize/Close, and the rail's collapse glyph) all still used hardcoded Unicode instead of the prototype's own SVGs. The exact paths for the LayerChrome partial (Expand/Pop out/Close) were not resolvable from the visible template source — they are decoded from the prototype's own gzip+base64 embedded resource bundle (design/prototype/Clio Session.html's line-379 manifest, key 774ac6dd-5309-49a6-896c-cfcd55579da9 -> LayerChrome.dc.html) rather than guessed, and that same decode revealed a real fact worth recording: the prototype's OWN Expand/Pop-out buttons carry no click handler at all in ANY of their five host windows (obs/files/run/bp/conf) — inert chrome even in the ground truth. This build's Expand is a real, working superset (it actually maximizes); Pop-out stays honestly disabled (no Tauri window API on web) rather than mimicking the prototype's silent no-op. Same-class sweep found and fixed one more: Modal.tsx's close button hugged a custom `header` instead of sitting at the far right (only the default title got the flex:1 that pushes it there) — affects the +new dialog, now fixed at the primitive so every future custom-header dialog gets it free. Settings' 13 placeholder pages (originally flagged here) are NOT re-verified in this pass — a parallel PASS 1 already fully built them under the dedicated 'settings' surface (docs/p5/conformance/settings.json); re-reporting them here would be stale/duplicate. Deleted the confirmed-dead CollapsiblePart.tsx (zero importers, superseded '›' glyph never reachable).

PASS 2 grind (2026-08-05): re-verified every remaining non-match item against the CURRENT tree and the live prototype (decoded, not guessed — via the prototype's own compiled React fiber tree at http://127.0.0.1:4399, and by driving its REAL send flow: session 1's own sendMain pushes straight into client-side mainQ, no backend involved). Found and fixed a real, previously-undetected defect: the message queue's container geometry had the DOM order backwards — Composer.tsx rendered the queue tray ABOVE the pill row, when the prototype always renders pill-then-tray-then-frame (confirmed live: pill border-radius 10px 10px 10px 0, tray border-radius 0px 14px 0px 0px — the tray's square top-left corner continues the pill's square bottom-left corner in one unbroken left edge). Reordered the JSX, corrected composer__queue's border-radius (was 14px 14px 0 0, now 0 14px 0 0) and margin-bottom, and corrected the header hint's exact text (mainQHint is 'main is mid-step · delivered at the next step boundary', a DIFFERENT prototype string from the per-row hint 'delivers at the next step boundary' — the app had collapsed both to the row string). This is now verified via a REAL side-by-side composite (screenshots/side-by-side/queue-panel.png), not just structurally: a new `queue` setup in side-by-side.mjs drives the prototype's own send flow for real (no mock), and drives the app's own real send flow too — with the two backend-mutating requests (PATCH mode, POST message) intercepted and held open in the browser (never fulfilled, never forwarded) so the real `sending` state stays true long enough to capture without ever reaching the shared live backend, honoring the read-only rule while still exercising real app code. The panel collapse/expand toggle item's residual half (the detail panel had no collapse-to-strip affordance at all) is now BUILT for real: DetailSlot.tsx gained a `collapsed` boolean (rightOpen/tgRight in the prototype) toggled by a new 'Collapse panel' button using a newly-added `panel-right` icon (the tgRight-shape family, divider at x=8.6, transcribed live from the same template block as the detail slot's Maximize button — distinct from the rail's `panel` icon at x=5.4), collapsing to a real 38px strip carrying only a '‹' re-expand button and a vertical kind-badge label (verbatim geometry decoded from the prototype's own rightClosed branch). It is entirely client-side layout state, self-contained in DetailSlot exactly like the existing `maximized` state, so it needed no new wiring — reachability of DetailSlot itself from the live transcript is still E7's separate, tracked gap. The download-button item was re-verified unchanged (still correctly the honest degraded pattern; relabeled from 'deviates' to 'unbacked' to match the settings.json convention for this exact scenario — icon fidelity fixed, backend route absent). The two settings cross-reference rows were re-checked against the current settings.json (36 match / 9 deviates / 1 missing / 1 unbacked of 47) — the 'deviates' rollup is still accurate and this file continues to defer to settings.json as the source of truth rather than duplicating its measurement.

PASS 3 grind (2026-08-05): re-verified every remaining non-match item against the current tree. Only one item was not 'match': the Download menu, which an independent audit had already corrected 'unbacked' -> 'not-wired' (clio-agent has served GET /v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}/export, RO-Crate lineage export, since 2026-07-22 (#973) — this build's disabled control was decorating a real, live-probed route, not documenting a genuine gap). Wired it for real per the audit's own direction: a new `Client.exportArtifact()` (apps/core) downloads the export bundle and the prototype's own three-row menu (download file / open storage location / copy link to artifact — transcribed verbatim from the plain, non-gzipped template this time, not decoded from the embedded bundle as PASS 1's note assumed was required) is now genuinely built in apps/web/src/detail/DetailSlot.tsx: two of the three rows are real (download triggers a browser download of the zip bytes; copy-link copies the real export URL), the third ('open storage location') stays the same honest degraded pattern already established for the window-chrome pop-out button, since no browser API opens the host OS file manager. A failed export surfaces a typed, visible error in the still-open menu rather than a silent no-op. Verified with a new real side-by-side composite (screenshots/side-by-side/detail-download.png, via a new `detail` setup in scripts/side-by-side.mjs) — geometry, colors and spacing match the prototype pixel-for-pixel, confirming the transcription. The two settings cross-reference rows were re-checked once more (47 items, 38 match / 9 deviates, unchanged from PASS 2) and are still correctly deferred to settings.json rather than duplicated here — genuinely out of this surface's scope, not left stale.

items.element: Send-while-busy message queue (reorder ↑/↓, in-place edit, remove, 'interrupt · deliver now' link)
items.proto_truth: Decoded from the prototype's own JS state (queueRows()/mainQ/mainQNow/sendTitle, design/prototype/Clio Session.html): while busy, Send enqueues instead of blocking (button title becomes 'Queue for the next step boundary', SAME arrow-up glyph). Each queued row is `#N` + text + a per-row hint ('delivers at the next step boundary' for #1, 'after message #N' otherwise), with four 20x20 icon-only controls: ↑ (mq.up, disabled at the top), ↓ (mq.down, disabled at the bottom), ✎ (mq.startEdit → an inline text input, save on blur/Enter, cancel on Escape — the prototype's own glyph is the pencil ✎, not scissors as an earlier draft of this row said), ✕ (mq.rm). A header row above the rows reads '{N} messages queued' (amber, uppercase) + a muted hint 'main is mid-step · delivered at the next step boundary' (a DIFFERENT string from the per-row hint) + a right-aligned 'interrupt and deliver' link (mainQNow/fv.deliverNow) titled 'Interrupt the current step and deliver immediately'. Container geometry, decoded live from the prototype's own computed styles: DOM order is pill row, then this tray, then the input frame (never tray-then-pill) — the pill's border-radius is 10px 10px 10px 0 (square bottom-left) and the tray's is 0px 14px 0px 0px (square top-left, only the top-right rounds), so the two share one unbroken square edge on the left.
items.app_evidence: apps/web/src/composer/Composer.tsx (QueuedMessage type, queuedMessages/onQueueMessage/onReorderQueuedMessage/onEditQueuedMessage/onRemoveQueuedMessage/onDeliverQueuedNow props, the composer__queue tray render block) + apps/web/src/session/SessionView.tsx (queue state, onDeliverQueuedNow calling the REAL client.cancelSession() then re-sending the held messages, and a useEffect that auto-delivers the next held message as soon as `sending` clears). PASS 2 fix: the tray rendered ABOVE the pill row in the JSX (backwards from the prototype's pill-then-tray-then-frame order) with both top corners rounded; reordered the JSX and corrected composer.css's border-radius/margin-bottom to the measured 0 14px 0 0, and corrected the header hint text (was reusing the row's 'delivers at the next step boundary' for both; now the header says the distinct 'main is mid-step · delivered at the next step boundary'). Locked by 7 tests in tests/unit/composer.test.tsx ('send-while-busy message queue', including 2 new PASS-2 tests for DOM order/border-radius and the exact header-vs-row hint text) and 2 end-to-end tests in tests/unit/session-view.test.tsx proving the real hold/auto-deliver and the real cancelSession() call. Verified visually via a REAL side-by-side composite (screenshots/side-by-side/queue-panel.png): a new `queue` setup in side-by-side.mjs drives the prototype's own real send flow (session 1's sendMain pushes straight into client-side mainQ, no mock, no backend) and the app's own real send flow (client.sendMessage/patchSession), with the app's two mutating requests intercepted and held open in the browser — never fulfilled, never forwarded to the shared live backend — purely to keep the real `sending` state true long enough to capture, honoring the read-only rule while exercising real code.
items.backend_surface: client-owned hold/reorder/edit/remove (correct — the prototype's own queue is client state, not a wire concept); deliver-now is REAL: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel via client.cancelSession(), confirmed present on SessionOperationsClient
items.fix_hint: Known, disclosed scope limit (unchanged by PASS 2): `busy` is this client's own send round-trip (POST -> load -> refreshPill), not the full multi-step turn the backend may still be running after that POST returns — there is no persistent live session-status subscription outside the observability panel (subscribeSessionTraceEvents only mounts when panel==='obs'). The queue behaves correctly for its own definition of busy; widening 'busy' to track the whole turn needs an always-on session-status feed, which is a distinct, larger project (touches App-level session refresh, not composer icons/buttons) — tracked as a follow-up, not silently narrowed.

items.element: Artifact/record detail panel toolbar: Download button / download menu
items.proto_truth: 24x24 button titled 'Download', svg 12x12 arrow-into-tray icon (`M6 1.5v6M3.2 5l2.8 2.8L8.8 5` + tray path). Triggers a small menu (tgArtMenu/popArtMenu) offering 'download file' / 'open storage location' / 'copy link to artifact' rows — transcribed verbatim from the plain (non-gzipped) template this pass: absolute panel at top:28px/right:0 of a `position:relative` wrapper spanning Copy+Download, min-width 180px, background var(--t-sf2), border 1px var(--t-bd35), radius 8px, padding 4px; each row is a full-width mono-12px button, padding 6px 9px, hover bg var(--t-hv). The prototype renders all three rows in the SAME (non-dimmed) text color — it does not visually distinguish the one row (open storage location) that has no browser-reachable target.
items.app_evidence: PASS 3 grind (2026-08-05): built the real menu per the independent audit's correction. apps/core adds `fetchArtifactExport`/`Client.exportArtifact()` (apps/core/src/client/artifact_export.ts, apps/core/src/client/http.ts) — GET /v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}/export, returning the raw zip Blob + the backend's Content-Disposition filename (falls back to `${id}.crate.zip`); locked by 3 new tests in apps/core/tests/session_endpoints.test.ts (URL, Content-Disposition filename, and a typed HttpError on 404 — never a silent empty download). apps/web/src/detail/DetailSlot.tsx gained an optional `client` prop and now renders the SAME three-row menu the prototype does (apps/web/src/detail/detail.css: `.detail__artifactactions`/`.detail__artmenurow`, geometry transcribed above via the kit Popover primitive): 'download file' calls `client.exportArtifact(record.id)` and triggers a real browser download (createObjectURL + a[download] + revoke — no page navigation); 'copy link to artifact' copies the real `{baseUrl}/v1/artifacts/{id}/export` URL to the clipboard; 'open storage location' is the one row with no browser-reachable target and stays the honest degraded pattern (disabled, dimmed, explanatory title) — the SAME documented, deliberate exception already used for the window-chrome pop-out button elsewhere in this file (ours states why nothing happens; the prototype's own inert rows don't). A failed export surfaces a typed inline error in the still-open menu (no silent fallback) rather than closing on failure. When no `client` is supplied the whole Download control degrades honestly (disabled, 'requires a live connection' title) instead of pretending a route it cannot reach — DetailSlot still has no live caller in the running app (E7, tracked separately, is the reachability gap, not this item). Locked by 6 new tests in apps/web/tests/unit/detail.test.tsx (menu contents, real download call + blob/anchor/revoke sequence, typed error stays open to retry, real clipboard link, open/close toggle, and the disabled open-storage-location row) plus the updated no-client test. Verified visually via a new real side-by-side composite (screenshots/side-by-side/detail-download.png; a new `detail` setup in scripts/side-by-side.mjs opens the SAME earthscope_stations.csv record on both sides — the prototype via its own artGo('earthscope_stations.csv') transcript-chip click, the app via the `?shell` fixture harness wired to a real client against the read-only live backend) — menu geometry/colors/spacing match pixel-for-pixel; the one visible difference is the deliberate open-storage-location dimming described above.
items.backend_surface: GET /v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}/export (real, clio-agent #973, wired end to end this pass) backs BOTH 'download file' and 'copy link to artifact'; 'open storage location' has no surface (desktop/OS file-manager concern, not a web-reachable route) and is the disclosed remaining wire gap
items.audit_correction: INDEPENDENT AUDIT of grind pass 2 (2026-08-05): corrected unbacked -> not-wired. The claim 'no artifact-content/download route confirmed on clio-agent' is FALSE and was false when written: clio-agent has served GET /v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}/export (hash-verified CAS/file bytes, src/clio_agent/gact/routes/artifact_export.py) since 2026-07-22 (#973), plus GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/artifacts and GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/export/bundle. Probed live against 127.0.0.1:17900 during this audit: a real artifact id returned 200 with 5,282 bytes. The disabled+titled control is therefore a dead control over a live route - 'download file' is wireable today (and 'copy link to artifact' can carry the export URL); only 'open storage location' still lacks a surface (desktop/OS concern). Counts as remaining work, not as an agreed degraded treatment. PASS 3 (2026-08-05) closed this out per the audit's own direction — see app_evidence.
